newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds open firmer amid overseas buying.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds open firmer amid overseas buying.

text.p: Canadian bonds opened stronger on Friday, following yesterday's sharp drop in prices, as the backup in yields helped draw foreign buyers into the market overnight, analysts said.

"It's normal for prices to rally a little bit from the lows. There was buying reported by some of the brokers overnight from both European and Asian accounts," said David Yu, a fixed-income porfolio manager with Perigee Investment Counsel.
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond rose C$0.36 to C$115.29 to yield 6.797 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond rose 4/32 to yield 6.77 percent. The spread between the bonds narrowed to three basis points from five basis points at Thursday's close.

Canadian bond prices tumbled on Thursday after the Bank of Canada surprised the market by raising its key bank rate by 25 basis points to 3.5 percent. It was the first rate hike by the bank in more than two years.
In addition to foreign buying prompted by the drop in prices, the Canadian market also benefited this morning from gains in U.S. Treasuries.
Analysts said activity in both markets was expected to be light for the rest of the session, particularly in Canada, which has the Canada Day market holiday on Tuesday.
The approaching meeting of the U.S. Federal Reserve's rate-setting Open Market Committee beginning on July 1 and the approach of quarter's end were also expected to help keep activity light.
In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bond rose C$0.22 to C$107.37 to yield 6.24 percent, compared to its U.S. equivalent, which rose 3/32 to yield 6.48 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds widened to 24 basis points from 23 basis points at Thursday's close.
The three-month cash T-bill yielded 3.13 percent against its U.S. equivalent. which yielded 5.12 percent.
